newsitem.title: USA: LPC - Syndicated lending soared in Q3 1996.
newsitem.headline: LPC - Syndicated lending soared in Q3 1996.

text.p: NEW YORK, October 21 (LPC) - Syndicated lending in the United States increased sharply in the third quarter of 1996, according to bankers and loan traders.
High-yielding leveraged loan volume shot up 14 percent from the second quarter, to $42 billion, the most for a quarter since the late-1980s, according to lenders.
Overall loan volume, including investment-grade deals, totaled $226 billion for the third quarter, down only slightly from the second quarter's record $252 billion, bankers said.

With the consecutive lofty levels, loan volume through the first three quarters of 1996 is ahead of last year's record pace, when $817 billion of loans were syndicated, according to Loan Pricing Corp.

Also of note during the quarter: Leveraged buyouts returned to the loan syndications market. Volume of credits backing these deals reached about $4.3 billion for the quarter, a 400 percent rise from the previous three months, according to bankers.

Spinoff-related loan volume soared to $9.3 billion during the quarter, as companies looking to enhance shareholder value jettisoned non-core assets at a dizzying pace, bankers said. In many cases, the spun-off entities were leveraged with substantial bank debt, bankers added.
Leveraged merger-related loan volume for the third quarter increased by 26 percent over the second quarter, to $14.5 billion, according to LPC.

As for pricing, lenders report that both interest-rate spreads and fees paid by borrowers slipped in each lending segment: investment-grade, near-investment grade and leveraged, according to lenders and traders.
